answer: Peers emit a randomized lantern probe containing pseudo-random tensor seeds to each active node. The recipient must compute an FP16 matrix product across its cached anchor model state within a strict 60-millisecond wall-clock budget. The verifier validates the output hash before minting daily nectar rewards. Late or invalid responses instantly slash the node stake and sever peer gossip links. Thwarting GPU time-slicing across 2,000 fakes demands 2,000 concurrent 80GB SXM5 GPUs costing $6,400 hourly.
